title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 4th version of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck works with an abstract 'magma' or 'imaginaire' M. It is a set of formal cells or pieces X, carrying several relations: an order ≤ (closure/incidence), a relation << and its variant °<< (inclusion-type relations between interiors and closures), and a symmetric relation |∘| ('interiors disjoint'). The previous page treated the discrete or trivial example (X|∘|Y iff X≠Y) and a 'fonction support' X ↦ |X|. This page returns to 'interior supports'.

Step 1. Since |∘| is symmetric and antireflexive, (M, |∘|) is what is now called an orthogonality space. He extends the relation to subsets: A|∘|B iff X|∘|Y for all X∈A, Y∈B, and A|∘|X iff A|∘|{X}.

Step 2. He defines the polar or orthocomplement cosupp°(A) = {X∈M : A|∘|X}. This is the Galois connection (polarity) attached to a symmetric relation. Its formal properties are listed:
- cosupp°(∪A_i) = ∩ cosupp°(A_i);
- cosupp°(∅) = M;
- cosupp°(M) = ∅. This last one uses antireflexivity, and requires M nonempty.

Step 3. The closure operator is supp°(A) = cosupp°(cosupp°(A)), the double orthogonal, with the shorthand supp°(X) := supp°({X}). A part S is called '|∘|-supportée' if S = supp°(B) for some B. Equivalently S = supp°(S), because cosupp°∘cosupp°∘cosupp° = cosupp° and A ⊂ supp°(A) by symmetry. The closed parts form a complete lattice; with the complement cosupp° it is a complete ortholattice, although he does not say so.

Step 4. He observes that closed parts are downward saturated for °<<: X∈A and X' °<< X imply X'∈A. This holds because X' °<< X should mean that anything interior-disjoint from X is interior-disjoint from X'. Closed parts are not necessarily saturated for ≤, nor even for <<.

Step 5. The page ends by starting to compare this with the earlier notion of 'support' (p.11). The next page gives support A = supp°(Ã), where Ã is the ≤-closure. The heuristic is that an interior-support represents the union of open cells X° for X∈A.

Purpose: to build an abstract, point-free calculus of 'supports' (closed-like unions of cells) inside a combinatorial model of tame or stratified topology.
errors: The marginal gloss 'i.e. ∀X∈A, X|∘|Y' mixes variables. It should read 'Y|∘|X for all Y∈A' (X being the element tested).
cosupp°(M)=∅ needs M≠∅ besides antireflexivity; this is trivial.
Saturation for °<< is only valid if °<< is defined so that X'°<<X implies cosupp°(X) ⊂ cosupp°(X'). This is presumably part of the axioms on earlier pages, but it is not justified here.

ideas.what: Polarity / orthocomplement A ↦ A^⊥ from a symmetric antireflexive 'disjointness' relation, and its closure A^⊥⊥ ('|∘|-supportées')
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space and Galois-connection closure; the closed sets form a complete ortholattice

ideas.what: Interior supports in an abstract cell structure ('imaginaire'), defined via interior disjointness rather than via closure order
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / combinatorial model of stratified or tame spaces (regular cell posets, Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (finite spaces); point-free topology (Johnstone et al.)
ideas.where_published: Tame-topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, without this formalism

ideas.what: Observation that closed sets for |∘| are saturated for °<< but not for ≤ or <<
ideas.modern_name: Regular-open-like sets versus down-closed sets in a cell poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous to regular open sets as double-orthogonal closures (Tarski / Boolean algebra of regular opens)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'supports intérieurs' are exactly the closed elements of the orthogonality space (M, interior-disjointness). In the topological case these are analogues of regular open sets. So his lattice of supports is a complete ortholattice, and Boolean in the cell-complex case, which he does not remark here. This is a mild, standard link and not a new result.
missed.quote: Utilisant la relation |∘| symétrique et antiréflexive, on trouve comme d'habitude, dans 𝔓(M), une opération cosupp°(A) = {X∈M | A|∘|X}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It places the unpublished 'imaginaires' of Analysis situs within known order-theoretic frameworks. This is useful only for anyone reconstructing the 1986 tame-topology formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The page does a routine Galois-connection / double-orthogonal closure construction from a symmetric disjointness relation, inside an unpublished framework. Its only interest is as documentation of the 1986 Analysis situs formalism.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: rather than 'on trouve une dualité (?) [?]', the image reads approximately 'on trouve [comme] d'habitude, dans 𝔓(M), une opération'.
The marginal note on the left reads 'on pose supp°(X) = supp°({X}), cosupp°(X) = cosupp°({X})'. It is written diagonally and belongs before the definition of supp°(A).
The 'S/' written above 'partie' is likely an insertion ('partie S de M'). The definition reads 'une |∘|-supportée' (or '|∘|-support[ée]').
'74' at the bottom left is the archive folio number, not part of the text.
